prompt: Why can Cloud Shell not reach a private address in the planner's VPC network?

choices.text: Cloud Shell blocks all outbound traffic
choices.why: It reaches the internet and Google's APIs.

choices.text: It lives in a project of Google's
choices.why: Right. It reaches private addresses no better than the internet does.

choices.text: The planner's firewall denies Cloud Shell's tag
choices.why: Cloud Shell is not in the network for a tag to matter.

choices.text: Private addresses need a VPN from every browser
choices.why: The point is where the machine is, not the browser.

prompt: `gcloud cloud-shell ssh` printed that automatic authentication is disabled. What does that protect?

choices.text: The SSH key
choices.why: The key is made either way.

choices.text: The placeholder token from being sent
choices.why: The token was sent, and refused.

choices.text: Cloud Shell's home directory
choices.why: The message is about credentials.

choices.text: Your own credentials, kept out
choices.why: Right. --authorize-session would send them; without it, the session is one fewer place they are.

prompt: What did gcloud create on the laptop the first time `cloud-shell ssh` ran?

choices.text: An SSH key pair for gcloud
choices.why: Right. It reuses it for every machine it connects to.

choices.text: A new gcloud configuration
choices.why: No configuration was created.

choices.text: A Cloud Shell home directory
choices.why: That would be on Google's side, and the request was refused.

choices.text: A service account key
choices.why: SSH keys are not service account keys.

prompt: Which service refused the lab's request to start Cloud Shell?
hint: Like every service in this course.

choices.text: SSH, for a missing key
choices.why: The key had just been made.

choices.text: The organisation policy disabling Cloud Shell
choices.why: The error is about authentication.

choices.text: The Cloud Shell API itself
choices.why: Right. UNAUTHENTICATED, with the placeholder token.

choices.text: The emulator
choices.why: The emulator is Pub/Sub only.

prompt: gcloud's command for copying files between Cloud Shell and the laptop is `gcloud cloud-shell ___`.
An engineer installs a package with apt in Cloud Shell on Monday. Is it there on Tuesday?

choices.text: Yes; Cloud Shell keeps the whole disk
choices.why: Only the home directory is kept.

choices.text: Yes, if the session was idle
choices.why: Idleness ends a session; it keeps nothing extra.

choices.text: No; only the home directory persists
choices.why: Right. Each session runs on a fresh machine.

choices.text: Only in ephemeral mode
choices.why: Ephemeral mode keeps even less.

prompt: How does the planner make `jq` and `dig` present in every Cloud Shell session?

choices.text: A script run at each start
choices.why: Right. It runs as root every time the machine starts.

choices.text: By installing them once with apt
choices.why: They would be gone next session.

choices.text: By asking Google to add them to the image
choices.why: The image is Google's; the customisation is yours.

choices.text: By copying the binaries into /usr/bin
choices.why: /usr/bin is outside ~ and is reset.

prompt: Why is Cloud Shell's home directory not a backup?

choices.text: It is erased at the end of each session
choices.why: It persists between sessions.

choices.text: It is shared with every user
choices.why: Each user has their own.

choices.text: It cannot hold more than ten files
choices.why: It is small in gigabytes, not in files.

choices.text: Long unused, it is deleted
choices.why: Right. It is scratch space that happens to last; what matters belongs in a repository or a bucket.

prompt: `du` reported `.local` and `gcp` in the lab's home. About how many megabytes did they hold together? Within 50.
What part of this course's lab would not survive a Cloud Shell session, even though the home directory fits?

choices.text: The Terraform binary in ~/.local/bin
choices.why: That is inside the home directory.

choices.text: The Java runtime, from apt
choices.why: Right. It is installed outside ~, which is what .customize_environment is for.

choices.text: The Python virtual environment
choices.why: It lives in ~/gcp/venv.

choices.text: gcloud's configurations
choices.why: They live under the home directory.

prompt: Who can open a Cloud Shell web preview address?

choices.text: Only you, through Google's proxy
choices.why: Right. It goes through Google's proxy, as you.

choices.text: Anybody with the address
choices.why: The address is authenticated as your account.

choices.text: Anyone in your organisation
choices.why: It is per user.

choices.text: Nobody; it only works on port 22
choices.why: It serves a web port, 8080 by default.

prompt: Why is pasting a script into Cloud Shell as risky as running it on the laptop of an engineer with production roles?

choices.text: Cloud Shell runs as a project owner
choices.why: It runs as you, with your roles.

choices.text: Scripts there skip IAM
choices.why: IAM applies to every call.

choices.text: It acts as you, with all your roles
choices.why: Right. With no confirmation, in every project.

choices.text: It has no audit log
choices.why: Calls are logged as from you.

prompt: A runbook step says *open Cloud Shell and run the rollback*. The organisation then disables Cloud Shell for its users. What should the runbook have said?
hint: Assume only what will be there.

choices.text: To re-enable Cloud Shell first
choices.why: That is an administrator's decision, not a step at night.

choices.text: What to type in any terminal with gcloud
choices.why: Right. Cloud Shell or a laptop; the runbook needs neither in particular.

choices.text: To use the console's buttons instead
choices.why: Screens change; a command is what can be written down.

choices.text: Nothing; disabling is temporary
choices.why: It lasts as long as the administrator wants.

prompt: Match each Cloud Shell limit to what it bounds.

pairs.right: a session with no home at all

right_distractors: the number of projects you see

prompt: Put what happens when a Cloud Shell session starts in order.
items: a fresh machine starts from Google's image
trap: Putting the script before the home directory is the slip: the script lives in the home directory, so the disk has to be attached first.

prompt: An engineer leaves a small web server running in Cloud Shell for a colleague to test overnight. What will the colleague find?

choices.text: The server, on a public address
choices.why: Nothing in Cloud Shell has a public address.

choices.text: The server, through the colleague's own preview
choices.why: The colleague's Cloud Shell is another machine.

choices.text: A copy of the server in the home directory
choices.why: Files persist; the running process does not.

choices.text: Nothing; it stopped
choices.why: Right. Processes stop with the machine, and web preview is authenticated as its owner.
